title: Lighthouse concierge intake and scope fractioning
creator: Priya Raman
description: Create a repeatable, signal-weighted concierge intake flow for Lighthouse/top accounts that: 1) deconflicts overlapping feature asks from multiple stakeholders, 2) assigns a scoped credit (fraction of full roadmap effort) for each committed item, and 3) exposes a clear commitment window and fallback to the public runway. This ticket covers the intake rubric, scoring model, commitment SLA, communication templates, and a lightweight console view for tracking active concierge requests. Goal: reduce ad-hoc escalations and unscoped promises while improving predictability for enterprise renewals.
acceptance_criteria: A deterministic scoring rubric (signal weights + thresholds) is documented and reviewed by Sales and CSMs
A scoped-credit model that maps customer ask sizes to 0.1/0.25/0.5/1.0 roadmap credits is defined
Communication templates (intake ack, scope confirmation, SLA breach fallback) live in Confluence
Console view prototype with active concierge queue and commitment window mock is available for PM/Eng review
Rollout plan (pilot with 3 Lighthouse accounts) and success metrics are defined
comments: 2025-07-15 Priya Raman: Created ticket after exec meeting. Initial ask from Sales included three concurrent feature requests from Account A and Account B. Need to ensure we don't double-commit.

2025-07-18 Jonah Martinez: Met with CSMs and AE reps. Proposed signals: ARR, renewal month proximity, legal/regulatory blocker, usage growth, and strategic reference value. Agreed to prototype weights and run historical backfill for validation.
2025-07-22 Data note (Eng): Backfill of last 18 months shows ARR and renewal proximity explain 72% of escalation resolution priority. Filing ENG-1842 for required dataset aggregation.
2025-07-25 Design feedback (Aisha Kapoor): UI should surface 'commit credit' and 'fallback runway' clearly—mock attached in Drive. Recommend a compact list and detail flyout for each concierge item.
2025-07-28 PM decision: Use four credit buckets (0.1, 0.25, 0.5, 1.0) aligned to expected engineering effort; credits are non-transferrable and expire at commitment window end.
2025-07-30 Legal input: Any commitment wording must include explicit fallbacks; drafted clause in Confluence. Assigned legal reviewer: Daniel Ortiz.

2025-08-02 Jonah Martinez: Pilot invites prepared for Account A, B, C. Pilot success metrics: commit-to-delivery accuracy > 80% over 90-day window, reduction in emergency escalations by 40% for participating accounts.

2025-08-04 Engineering estimate arrived: Backend ticket for console + scoring service estimated 6 sprints across a small squad. Need to negotiate scope to fit 2-sprint pilot MVP. Opened dependency ENG-2719 for MVP scope reduction planning.
decision_log: Use composite signal model instead of purely ARR-first to avoid over-indexing on raw revenue
Adopt credit buckets to allow partial commitments and preserve roadmap flexibility
Pilot will be timeboxed to 90 days with three lighthouse accounts before any broader rollouts
follow_up_tasks: Finalize signal weights and run historical validation by 2025-08-12
Convene Legal + Sales to finalize customer-facing SLA language by 2025-08-10
Trim console MVP scope and re-estimate engineering effort (target 2-sprint MVP)
Prepare pilot onboarding checklist and CSM training materials
